rationale: D1, data-informed (not zero-shot): the first candidate of the multistate droplet spec for methanol, written after studying the experiment and the train runs. The train data show two extinction mechanisms that the first-generation model blurred into one: droplets below a critical diameter burn to a diffusive extinction at De/D0 near 0.5 whatever their size, droplets above it lose the flame to radiation about 0.9 of a diffusion-clock unit after ignition, and droplets far above it never establish a flame. The critical diameter falls from about 9 mm in air to 2.3 mm at 12 % O2 and is lowered by CO2 and helium. Rate law: hinge network on train plateau rates with a heat-up that scales with D0^2. Post-extinction evaporation decays from 0.06-0.08 to 0.02 mm2/s. Numbers typed from train tables by the author; no fit, no search.
